comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current EWI 2026–2027 OER Article 14A (2024-and-later ordinary Applied Mathematics examination programme) and Article 15 were freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. They control over generic webpage summaries and the public programme-facts API, which does not establish the full course table. The ordinary degree has twelve first-year 5-EC positions (60), ten second-year required 5-EC units plus two elective units (60), and a 30-EC minor, three 5-EC electives and TW3-01 Bachelor Project 15 EC in year three (60). Proof Techniques combines formal TW1-11T theory 3 EC and TW1-11P practical 2 EC, counted once as 5; TW1-11T/P is not asserted as a catalogue code. Exactly one of the five electives must be non-mathematical. The neutral selection is the first four distinct mathematical table entries TW-E01 Advanced Statistics, TW-E02 Machine Learning, TW-E03 Markov Processes and TW-E04 Graph Theory, plus the first non-mathematical entry TW-E99 Algorithm Design, all 5 EC. E01 is represented in year-two Q3 and E99 in year-two Q4; E02/E03/E04 are represented in year-three Q3, and the project can use its formal Q4 period. This follows published teaching periods without certifying future timeslots or timetable compatibility. Students must consider required prior knowledge; Article 15 grants unconditional access to other TW units. Project entry requires all first-year courses and at least 40 major EC from years two and three, with topic-specific essential foundations subject to the programme director. The genuine 30-EC minor must meet approval and non-overlap rules and cannot duplicate the five electives. No double-bachelor requirements or second set of alternatives is added.

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, computation & quantitative systems
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, probability and numerical methods through optimisation, algorithms, statistical learning and models of technical and societal systems. This is a broad applied quantitative response; it does not reproduce Delft's proof-intensive specialist mathematics sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines six dedicated mathematical-method courses with algorithms, optimisation, data methods and four economic-system applications; the label does not claim the missing proof-intensive pure-mathematics sequence.
progression: All formal prerequisites and exact Fall 2026-start availability were checked against the current workbook. Programming precedes algorithmic work; Algorithms and Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms; Mathematical Methods precedes all dependent mathematics and neural-network study. Numerical methods precede Advanced Calculus because of the published timetable. The optimisation course follows programming; no additional prerequisite is invented.

selection.assessment: All 16 generator-eligible interests describe the same integrated applied-mathematics core: mathematical structures and reasoning, modelling, algorithms, optimisation, uncertainty, statistics and technical or societal applications. The curriculum already implements those strands. Topic-level examples such as mathematical physics, operations research and differential-equation applications may inform course choices but cannot independently generate another alternative. A second curriculum would require an arbitrary application choice unsupported by a distinct generator-eligible direction, so production stops at one.

notes.text: Delft Applied Mathematics includes a cumulative proof-intensive sequence in analysis, measure-theoretic probability, abstract algebra, partial differential equations and mathematical modelling. The UCR programme combines mathematical methods with computation, statistics and quantitative applications; it does not reproduce that specialist mathematics sequence.
